- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict early spikes; correct by adding 10–30% to initial forecast values.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model overreacts to short-term noise; dampen early forecast peaks and delay peak prediction by 2–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes after 10–15 day horizons; apply a 15–25% upward bias for 15+ day forecasts.
- After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often overshoots or fails to capture sustained momentum; adjust by reducing forecast slope after peak and adding 5–10% lagged sentiment-weighted correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated oscillation (alternating +/–), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; apply a 5–10% upward adjustment to forecast mean for 10+ day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently underestimates tail risk; add 10–20% buffer to final 5–7 days of forecast if sentiment is positive or volatile.
